title: Declaration of Independence
summary: The Congress of Tucumán declared the independence of the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata from Spanish rule.
significance: The declaration marked a defining milestone in the process of establishing an independent political community.

title: Provincial Autonomy
summary: Political authority became fragmented among provinces following the collapse of the central government.
significance: Provincial autonomy and disagreements about federalism shaped subsequent efforts to organize the country.

title: Rise of Juan Manuel de Rosas
summary: Juan Manuel de Rosas became governor of Buenos Aires and a dominant figure in regional politics.
significance: His influence reflected continuing conflicts over political authority, federalism and national organization.

title: Constitution of 1853
summary: Representatives of the Argentine Confederation adopted a constitution establishing a federal framework.
significance: The constitution became a foundation of Argentina's national political institutions. Buenos Aires initially remained outside the Confederation.

title: National Political Unification
summary: Bartolomé Mitre assumed the presidency after the political reunification of Buenos Aires and the Confederation.
significance: National authorities consolidated institutions, although conflict and territorial expansion continued.

title: Buenos Aires Becomes the Federal Capital
summary: Buenos Aires was federalized and established as the national capital.
significance: The decision helped resolve a major dispute over the relationship between the capital and the provinces.

title: Immigration and Export Growth
summary: Agricultural exports, railways, urbanization and large-scale immigration transformed Argentine society.
significance: Export-led growth connected Argentina more closely to international markets while changing its population and cities.

title: Sáenz Peña Electoral Reform
summary: Electoral reform established secret and compulsory voting for Argentine male citizens within the system's eligibility rules.
significance: The reform helped broaden electoral participation and changed national political competition.

title: Yrigoyen Becomes President
summary: Hipólito Yrigoyen of the Radical Civic Union assumed the presidency after the 1916 election.
significance: His election marked a major shift in electoral politics following the reforms of the preceding years.

title: Military Coup of 1930
summary: A military coup overthrew President Hipólito Yrigoyen.
significance: The coup initiated a prolonged period of political instability and weakened democratic continuity.

title: First Perón Presidency
summary: Juan Domingo Perón began his first presidential term after winning the 1946 election.
significance: Peronism reshaped labor politics, social policy, political identity and debates about the role of the state.

title: Women's Suffrage
summary: Law 13,010 recognized women's right to vote and participate in national elections.
significance: Women voted in a national election for the first time in 1951, expanding democratic participation.

title: Overthrow of Perón
summary: A military uprising overthrew President Juan Domingo Perón.
significance: Political exclusion, conflict over Peronism and military intervention contributed to decades of instability.

title: Military Dictatorship Begins
summary: A coup established the military government known as the National Reorganization Process.
significance: State terrorism, forced disappearances, torture and repression left a profound legacy in Argentine society.

title: Falklands/Malvinas War
summary: Argentina and the United Kingdom fought a war over the Falkland Islands, known in Argentina as the Islas Malvinas.
significance: Argentina's defeat further undermined the military government and accelerated the return to constitutional democracy.

title: Return to Democracy
summary: Raúl Alfonsín won the 1983 presidential election, restoring elected civilian government.
significance: The democratic transition opened a new period of constitutional government and efforts to address dictatorship-era human rights abuses.

title: Economic and Political Crisis
summary: A deep economic crisis culminated in sovereign debt default, banking restrictions and widespread protests.
significance: The crisis exposed serious weaknesses in the economic model and led to major political changes.

title: Javier Milei Assumes the Presidency
summary: Javier Milei took office as president and pursued fiscal adjustment, deregulation and changes to the state's economic role.
significance: His administration intensified national debates about inflation, public spending, social protections and economic reform.
